prompt: Which consumer product classification fits each purchase?

cases.text: A student grabs a pack of gum at the checkout without looking at other brands.
cases.explanation: It is bought frequently, immediately, and with minimal comparison and buying effort.

cases.text: A shopper visits three stores to compare winter coats on warmth, price, and style.
cases.explanation: The buyer compares alternatives carefully on suitability, quality, price, and style.

cases.text: A buyer waits eight months for one particular luxury watch brand and will not accept a substitute.
cases.explanation: Strong brand identification leads the buyer to make a special purchase effort.

cases.text: A salesperson calls about a pre-paid funeral plan that the family had never thought of buying.
cases.explanation: Unsought products are items the consumer either does not know about or does not normally think of buying.

cases.text: A parent picks up laundry detergent at a corner grocery store on the way home.
cases.explanation: Laundry detergent is a low-priced item placed in widespread locations and bought frequently with minimal effort.

cases.text: A couple spends two weekends comparing sofas at furniture showrooms before choosing one.
cases.explanation: Furniture is purchased less frequently and compared carefully across fewer outlets with deeper sales support.

prompt: Put the five stages of the Product Life Cycle (PLC) in order, from first to last.

steps.explanation: The company first finds and develops a new product idea while sales are zero and investment costs mount.
Next, the product is introduced in the market, with slow sales growth and heavy launch expenses.
After introduction, rapid market acceptance and increasing profits follow as early and later buyers adopt the product.
Growth gives way to maturity once most potential buyers have accepted the product.
Decline is the final stage, when sales fall off and profits drop.

prompt: A snack company is developing a new protein bar. Which of the first four new product development steps is each moment?

cases.text: Engineers, salespeople, suppliers, and customers submit 300 suggestions for new snack products.
cases.explanation: Step 1 is the systematic search for new product ideas from internal and external sources.

cases.text: The product committee drops every idea that is not real, winnable, and worth doing, leaving five candidates.
cases.explanation: Step 2 spots good ideas and drops poor ones early using structured criteria.

cases.text: A detailed description of the bar stated in meaningful consumer terms is shown to twenty target gym-goers to gauge their reactions.
cases.explanation: Step 3 turns the idea into a product concept and presents it to target consumers.

cases.text: The team writes a statement specifying the target market, planned value proposition, first-year sales goals, and long-run marketing mix.
cases.explanation: Step 4 designs an initial marketing strategy for introducing the product to the market.

prompt: Sort each new product development activity by whether AI can accelerate it directly or whether it still requires real-world suppliers and paying customers.

bins.label: Accelerated by AI in early or design steps
Requires real suppliers and real paying customers

cards.text: Mining thousands of online customer complaints and patent filings to propose candidate product ideas
cards.explanation: In Step 1 (idea generation), generative AI can synthesize reviews, complaints, and patents in minutes.

cards.text: Creating rapid visual concept renderings and pretesting wording on synthetic AI personas
cards.explanation: In Step 3 (concept development and testing), AI accelerates visual mockups and preliminary wording checks.

cards.text: Using generative design and coding assistants to iterate prototype geometry and software interfaces
cards.explanation: In Step 6 (product development), computer-aided generative design and coding tools speed up prototype iteration.

cards.text: Verifying actual unit manufacturing costs and supplier quotes for business analysis
cards.explanation: Step 5 (business analysis) depends on real supplier cost data that cannot be simulated away.

cards.text: Measuring actual retail shelf acceptance and repeat purchase rates in a test market
cards.explanation: Step 7 (test marketing) requires real retail settings and real paying customers.

cards.text: Executing regional or international commercialization with retail distribution partners
cards.explanation: Step 8 (commercialization) introduces the actual product into real markets.

question_text: In a blind taste test, shoppers rate two colas equally. When the brand labels are revealed, they rate one cola much higher and say they are willing to pay a premium for it. What concept explains this difference?
hint: The physical drink did not change. Only knowing the brand name changed the response.
correct_answer_citation: Week 7: Brand Equity and Brand Sponsorship

options.option_explanation: Correct. Brand equity is the differential effect that knowing the brand name has on customer response to the product or its marketing.
A private (or store) brand is created and owned by a reseller. It does not explain the differential response to knowing a brand name.
Conformance quality measures how consistently a product delivers its targeted level of performance, which was identical in the blind test.
Concept testing evaluates a new product concept before development, whereas these colas are existing products.

prompt: Match each service characteristic with the situation and marketing response that illustrates it.

pairs.match: A dental clinic displays staff credentials and spotless treatment rooms so patients can see signals of quality before treatment.
pairs.explanation: Because services cannot be seen or felt before purchase, marketers manage the evidence with concrete signals of quality.

pairs.match: A haircut is produced and consumed at the same moment, making the stylist-client interaction part of the service itself.
pairs.explanation: Services cannot be separated from their providers and are produced and consumed simultaneously.

pairs.match: Two baristas at the same cafe prepare lattes of different quality depending on the morning rush.
pairs.explanation: Service quality depends on who provides the service and when, where, and how it is provided.

pairs.match: A hotel charges lower room rates on Tuesday nights because an unsold room tonight cannot be stored for Saturday.
pairs.explanation: Services cannot be stored for later sale or use, so firms use differential pricing or reservations to match supply and demand.

question_text: An airline deploys an LLM-based customer-service agent that handles 5,000 concurrent rebooking chats during a snowstorm at 3:00 a.m. However, two passengers asking the exact same baggage-fee question receive slightly different explanations. Which pair of service characteristics does this scenario highlight?
hint: Consider how cloud software changes capacity limits and how probabilistic language models behave across runs.
correct_answer_citation: Week 7: How Artificial Intelligence Reshapes the Four Service Characteristics

options.option_text: Flexible capacity under perishability, paired with probabilistic output variability across runs
options.option_explanation: Correct. Cloud-hosted AI scales concurrent capacity during demand spikes and operates at any hour, while large language models remain probabilistic and can return different answers to the identical question across runs.

options.option_text: Complete elimination of service intangibility and service inseparability
options.option_explanation: AI services remain intangible before use and are still produced and consumed simultaneously during the customer's conversation.

options.option_text: Rigid shift-based capacity limits and identical deterministic outputs on every run
options.option_explanation: AI delivery is separated from human labor shifts, and large language models are probabilistic rather than strictly identical across runs.

options.option_text: Physical inventory storage of services for later resale
options.option_explanation: Even with elastic cloud capacity, a service interaction is still produced and consumed live rather than stored in physical inventory.
